title: Remote inspector throws error when using custom class_name (extending any Node) in typed dictionary
body:
### Tested versions

Occured in 4.4.1.stable. Will test more later on.

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 26 Mar 2025 07:48:57 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi, renoir, ACO, DRM 3.61, 6.14.0-1-MANJARO) - AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads)

### Issue description

When viewing a typed-dictionary in the remote inspector with a custom class (with custom class_name), the inspector throws an error. However, this only happens when the referenced object is inside the tree.

```E 0:00:03:055   get_script: Caller thread can't call this function in this node (/root/Main/@ColorRect@2). Use call_deferred() or call_thread_group() instead.
  <C++ Error>   Condition "!is_accessible_from_caller_thread()" is true. Returning: (Variant())
  <C++ Source>  scene/main/node.cpp:3989 @ get_script()
E 0:00:03:055   validate_object: Attempted to getptr an object into a TypedDictionary.Key, that does not inherit from 'GDScript'.
  <C++ Error>   Condition "other_script.is_null()" is true. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  ./core/variant/container_type_validate.h:145 @ validate_object()
E 0:00:03:055   encode_variant: Parameter "value" is null.
  <C++ Source>  core/io/marshalls.cpp:1865 @ encode_variant()
E 0:00:03:055   encode_variant: Condition "err" is true. Returning: err
  <C++ Source>  core/io/marshalls.cpp:1895 @ encode_variant()
E 0:00:03:055   encode_variant: Condition "err" is true. Returning: err
  <C++ Source>  core/io/marshalls.cpp:1895 @ encode_variant()
E 0:00:03:055   encode_variant: Condition "err" is true. Returning: err
  <C++ Source>  core/io/marshalls.cpp:1895 @ encode_variant()
E 0:00:03:055   encode_variant: Condition "err" is true. Returning: err
  <C++ Source>  core/io/marshalls.cpp:1895 @ encode_variant()
E 0:00:03:055   _write_out: Condition "err != OK || size > out_buf.size() - 4" is true. Continuing.
  <C++ Source>  core/debugger/remote_debugger_peer.cpp:108 @ _write_out()

```

Some notes:

- Does *NOT* happen with typed arrays
- Using the base-class to type the dictionary is fine (in the MRP using ColorRect would be fine)
- It works when *NOT* having the referenced node inside the tree
- This does not stop the code from working like expected, it seems to be only an issue with the (remote) inspector

The inspector will not be able to show information about the selected node, it will remain on the previous node. I suppose the error aborts the current selection action.

Looking through the code, it seems to not be able to call get_script() on the dictionary key, resulting in the check at line 145 failing?
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/215acd52e82f4c575abb715e25e54558deeef998/core/variant/container_type_validate.h#L145

### Steps to reproduce

Create a script to extend an existing node (like `ColorRect`)
Give it a class_name (i.e. `PremiumColorRect`).

Create a node in the tree, add a script, add a typed dictionary using the class_name as key
`var typed_dict: Dictionary[PremiumColorRect, String] = {}`

 In code (for example in `_ready()`) create a new `PremiumColorRect` and add it to the dictionary as key (with any value).
Add the created `PremiumColorRect` as a child.

Run the scene, try to inspect the node in the remote inspector.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[custom_class_typed_dictionary_MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19732227/custom_class_typed_dictionary_MRP.zip)
